stories.headline: Adaption Launches AutoScientist, an AI Tool That Automates the Model-Training Research Loop

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Adaption introduced AutoScientist, a system that automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment by co-optimizing training data and model recipes until quality converges on the user's objective.
CEO Sara Hooker, formerly VP of AI research at Cohere, said the tool co-optimizes both data and model and 'suggests we can finally allow for successful frontier AI trainings outside of these labs.'

Adaption says AutoScientist more than doubled win-rates across different models, with aggregate win-rate rising from 48% to 64% when AutoScientist was used instead of an AI researcher's recommendation.

AutoScientist builds on Adaption's existing Adaptive Data product and is being offered free for the first 30 days after release; conventional benchmarks like SWE-Bench or ARC-AGI do not apply because the system adapts models to specific tasks.

stories.headline: Claude Mythos Preview Becomes First AI to Complete Both of UK AISI's Cyber Ranges

key_facts.fact: A newer Claude Mythos Preview checkpoint became the first AI model to complete both of the UK AI Security Institute's cyber ranges, which simulate cyberattacks on small, undefended enterprise networks.
The checkpoint solved the 32-step corporate network attack range 'The Last Ones' in 6 of 10 attempts and the previously unsolved operational-technology range 'Cooling Tower' in 3 of 10 attempts.
OpenAI's GPT-5.5 solved 'The Last Ones' in 3 of 10 attempts and did not complete 'Cooling Tower'.

AISI estimated in February 2026 that the length of cyber tasks frontier models can complete had been doubling every 4.7 months since late 2024, down from an 8-month estimate in November 2025; Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 substantially exceeded both trends.
AISI's cyber range experiments give each model a budget of up to 100 million tokens per attempt, and recent models disproportionately benefit from higher token limits.

stories.headline: Anthropic on Track for $50B Revenue Run Rate; Overtakes OpenAI in Business Adoption

key_facts.fact: Investor documents show Anthropic's revenue run rate is on track to hit $50 billion by the end of June, up sharply from an original full-year target of about $30 billion ARR.
Spend-management firm Ramp says more of its customers now use Anthropic than OpenAI, the first time Anthropic has led in business adoption.

The May Ramp AI Index put business adoption at 34.4% for Anthropic versus 32.3% for OpenAI, with OpenAI losing 2.9 points and Anthropic gaining 3.8 points in April while the total market grew just 0.2 points.

stories.headline: Anthropic Restores Third-Party Agent Access With New Agent SDK Credits Starting June 15

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Anthropic announced a new 'Agent SDK' credit category for paid Claude subscribers, reversing its April 2026 policy that had barred third-party agents like OpenClaw from running on Claude subscriptions.

Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage will no longer count toward a plan's regular usage limits; eligible Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users instead claim a separate monthly credit.
Monthly Agent SDK credit amounts are $20 for Pro, $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, $20 for Team Standard seats, $100 for Team Premium seats, and $20 to $200 for Enterprise plans.

The credit covers the Agent SDK, the `claude -p` non-interactive command, the Claude Code GitHub Actions integration, and third-party apps that authenticate with a Claude subscription; API key users are unaffected and keep pay-as-you-go billing.
The April 2026 prohibition was introduced after some subscribers paying $20 to $200 per month consumed hundreds or thousands of dollars of tokens through OpenClaw and similar autonomous agents.

stories.headline: Blackstone Raises $1.75B in IPO of Data Center REIT BXDC

key_facts.fact: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust priced its IPO at $20 per share on May 13, selling 87.5 million shares to raise $1.75 billion; the REIT will trade on the NYSE under ticker BXDC starting May 14.
The vehicle will target newly built data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion leased to investment-grade hyperscalers; it has not yet acquired any assets, making it a 'blind pool.'
BXDC plans to buy data centers in hubs including Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland and Austin, and targets returns of 5.75% to 7% or higher.
If the underwriters' 30-day option is exercised in full, gross proceeds would reach $2.0 billion; the offering is led by Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, among others.

stories.headline: Cerebras Prices IPO at $185, Above Range, Raising $5.55B at $56.4B Valuation

key_facts.fact: Cerebras Systems priced its IPO at $185 per share on May 13, above the marketed range of $150-$160, selling 30 million Class A shares to raise $5.55 billion.
At the IPO price, Cerebras is valued at $56.43 billion on a fully diluted basis, making it the largest US stock market debut so far in 2026.
The final price marks a sharp escalation from Cerebras's earlier marketing: it first disclosed a $115-$125 range on May 4 and a $23 billion valuation in a February funding round.
Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14 under ticker CBRS; underwriters hold a 30-day option for an additional 4.5 million shares.
Co-founder and CEO Andrew Feldman holds a stake worth about $1.9 billion at the IPO price.

stories.headline: Cerebras Prices IPO at $185 a Share, Raising $5.55B in Year's Largest Debut

key_facts.fact: Cerebras Systems priced its US IPO at $185 per share on May 13, above the marketed $150-$160 range, selling 30 million shares to raise $5.55 billion.
The pricing implies a fully diluted valuation of $56.43 billion, making it the largest stock market debut so far in 2026.

The offering was heavily oversubscribed, with investors placing orders for more than 20 times the shares available; Cerebras had raised its range from an earlier $115-$125 and upsized from 28 million shares.

Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14 under the ticker 'CBRS', with the offering set to close May 15; underwriters also have a 30-day option for up to 4.5 million additional shares.

stories.headline: Cisco Posts Record Q3 Revenue, Cuts Nearly 4,000 Jobs in AI Restructuring

key_facts.fact: Cisco reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $15.8 billion, up 12% year over year, with GAAP net income of $3.4 billion ($0.85/share, up 35%) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.06, up 10%.

Cisco announced a restructuring plan on May 13 that will reduce its workforce in Q4 by fewer than 4,000 jobs, representing less than 5% of its total employee base, with notifications beginning May 14.
Cisco expects pre-tax restructuring charges of up to $1 billion, recognizing about $450 million in Q4 fiscal 2026 and the remainder in fiscal 2027.
Cisco raised its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast to $62.8 billion-$63 billion from a prior $61.2 billion-$61.7 billion, helped by a surge in hyperscaler orders for AI infrastructure.
Cisco now expects about $9 billion in FY2026 AI orders, up from a prior estimate of $5 billion; shares rose roughly 20% in after-hours trading.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Two First-in-Class Cancer Therapies, Beqalzi and Inqovi-Venetoclax Combo

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval to BeOne Medicines' Beqalzi (sonrotoclax), the first BCL2 inhibitor for adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of therapy including a BTK inhibitor.
Beqalzi's approval was supported by a Phase 1/2 study showing a 52% overall response rate, a 16% complete response rate, and a median duration of response of 15.8 months.
Beqalzi is the 14th novel drug approval of 2026, per the FDA's Novel Drug Approvals list, approved 5/13/2026.

Separately on May 13, the FDA approved Taiho Oncology's Inqovi (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax, the first all-oral combination regimen for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia in patients 75 or older or ineligible for intensive chemotherapy.
In the supporting trial, the Inqovi-venetoclax combination produced a 41.6% complete remission rate and a median overall survival of 15.5 months.

stories.headline: Foxconn Q1 Profit Rises 18.5% to $1.58B as AI Server Demand Surges

key_facts.fact: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) reported Q1 2026 net profit of T$49.92 billion ($1.58 billion), up 18.5% year-on-year and above Bloomberg estimates of T$48.43 billion, in results released May 14.
Q1 revenue jumped nearly 30% year-on-year to T$2.13 trillion (about $66.6 billion), a record, driven by AI server demand.
For the first time, Foxconn's cloud and networking division, which assembles AI server racks, accounted for 41% of total revenue, surpassing the consumer electronics segment at 35%.
Foxconn is a key supplier to Nvidia, assembling its most advanced AI servers, and expects operations to grow both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year in Q2 on AI-related products.

stories.headline: UK Inference Chip Startup Fractile Raises $220M Series B at ~$1B Valuation

key_facts.fact: UK-based AI inference chip startup Fractile closed a $220 million Series B round, announced May 13.

The round was co-led by Accel, Factorial Funds and Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, with participation from Conviction, Gigascale, O1A, Felicis, Buckley Ventures and 8VC; it values Fractile at around $1 billion.
Founded in 2022 by an Oxford PhD, Fractile builds chips and systems designed to overcome performance bottlenecks in large-scale AI inference; it had previously raised $17.5 million.
Fractile will use the funding to accelerate commercialization and deploy its first chips to customers, expanding hiring across offices in London, Bristol, San Francisco and Taipei.

stories.headline: LinkedIn to Cut About 5% of Staff in Latest Tech-Sector Layoffs

key_facts.fact: LinkedIn planned to inform staff of layoffs on May 13, cutting about 5% of its more than 17,500 full-time workers as it reorganizes teams toward growing business areas.

CEO Daniel Shapero told employees in a memo the reductions would impact engineering, product, marketing and the Global Business Organization, and that LinkedIn is scaling back marketing campaigns, vendor spend and underutilized office space.
The company is closing an office in Graz, Austria as part of the reorganization.
Sources said the layoffs were not driven by AI replacing jobs, though they come as US employers cited AI as the top reason for cuts for a second straight month.
LinkedIn's revenue rose 12% in the just-ended quarter from a year prior, according to parent Microsoft's securities filings.

stories.headline: Microsoft in Talks to Acquire Diffusion-LLM Startup Inception as It Hedges Against OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on May 13, citing five sources, that Microsoft has been quietly canvassing AI startups for acquisitions or strategic deals to build the option to operate independently of OpenAI.

Microsoft is in active talks with Inception, a Palo Alto startup spun out of Stanford by professor Stefano Ermon that builds diffusion-based language models processing tokens in parallel rather than one at a time.
Inception is seeking an acquisition price of more than $1 billion, and SpaceX has also courted the startup.

Microsoft's M12 fund participated in Inception's $50 million round last November; earlier this spring Microsoft weighed acquiring Cursor but backed away over antitrust concerns tied to its ownership of GitHub Copilot.
Microsoft's MAI Superintelligence team, set up in November 2025 under Mustafa Suleyman, shipped its first three foundation models in April, with a frontier general-purpose LLM targeted for 2027.

stories.headline: Rivian CEO's Mind Robotics Raises $400M Led by Kleiner Perkins for AI Manufacturing Robots

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Mind Robotics announced a $400 million financing led by Kleiner Perkins, bringing total investment in the company to more than $1 billion.

New investors include Meritech Capital, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Incharge Capital, A-Star Capital and Garuda Ventures, alongside existing investors Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Prysm Capital, Bain Capital Ventures and Greenoaks.
The round follows a $115 million seed financing in late 2025 and a $500 million Series A in March 2026.
Mind Robotics, founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe, builds AI-powered robots for manufacturing tasks and raised the round at a $3.4 billion valuation, according to a source.

stories.headline: Russian Parliament Passes Bill Allowing Putin to Order Invasions of Foreign Countries

key_facts.fact: Russia's parliament approved a bill on May 13 that allows President Vladimir Putin to order the invasion of foreign countries.

The bill legally permits Moscow to send troops abroad to protect Russian citizens who are arrested, investigated, put on trial or abused by foreign states, international courts and organizations Russia doesn't belong to.
Putin has 14 days to sign the bill into law.
Ukraine criticized the measure, with a foreign ministry spokesman saying the State Duma had decided to act as a 'factory for legalizing political adventures, occupation and terror.'

stories.headline: US Has Cleared ~10 Chinese Firms to Buy Nvidia H200, But No Chips Have Shipped

key_facts.fact: The US has cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's H200 AI accelerator, but not a single chip has been delivered, according to three people briefed on the licences, first reported by Reuters on May 14.

The US Commerce Department licences cover Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com, alongside distributors including Lenovo and Foxconn, with each cleared customer permitted to buy up to 75,000 H200 units.
Chinese buyers have held back after Beijing told domestic tech firms to pause H200 orders and pushed a parallel supply-chain security review to reduce dependence on US chips.

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told a Senate hearing that the Chinese government has inhibited the purchases to protect its domestic chip industry; the Trump deal also requires 25% of chip-sale revenue to be paid to the US.

stories.headline: US Clears Nvidia H200 Sales to ~10 Chinese Firms, but No Deliveries Yet

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department has approved around 10 Chinese companies, including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com, to buy Nvidia's H200 AI chips, plus distributors including Lenovo and Foxconn.
Each approved customer can purchase up to 75,000 chips under the US licensing terms, buying directly from Nvidia or through intermediaries.
Not a single delivery has been made; Chinese firms pulled back after guidance from Beijing as the government prioritizes a self-sufficient domestic chip industry.
Under an arrangement negotiated by Trump, the US would receive 25% of revenue from the chip sales, a structure requiring the chips to pass through US territory before shipment to China.
US rules issued in January require Chinese buyers to demonstrate they have installed sufficient security procedures and would not use the chips for military purposes.
